emails.subject: Action Required: Slow Recruitment at Site 203 (Dr. Ames) - Study INP-301
emails.body:
Hi David,

I'm writing to flag a concern regarding the patient recruitment pace at Site 203 (Dr. Ames) for the INP-301 study. They are significantly behind our enrollment targets for this quarter, having only screened 5 patients in the last month with 1 randomized.

Could you please take the following actions this week?

1.  Conduct a thorough review of the site's screening and enrollment log in the EDC. I'm particularly interested in any trends related to screen failure reasons.
2.  Proactively reach out to Dr. Ames and his study coordinator to schedule a call to discuss the recruitment challenges they are facing. We need to understand their barriers and collaboratively identify potential mitigation strategies (e.g., refining pre-screening, patient outreach, etc.).

Please let me know what you find in the screening log and when you have the call scheduled.

Thanks,

Sarah Chen
Clinical Trial Manager
Innovate Pharma

emails.subject: Re: Action Required: Slow Recruitment at Site 203 (Dr. Ames) - Study INP-301
emails.body:
Hi Sarah,

Thanks for flagging this. I've completed an initial review of the screening log for Site 203.

It appears the primary reason for screen failure is Exclusion Criterion #5 (HbA1c > 8.5%), which accounted for 12 of the 18 screen failures in the past 90 days. I've attached a brief summary for your reference.

I have already contacted the site coordinator and have a call scheduled with her and Dr. Ames for this Friday, Oct 28th, at 2:00 PM EST to discuss this trend and other potential recruitment barriers.

I will provide you with a summary of our discussion and the proposed action plan following the call.

Best regards,

David Miller
Clinical Research Associate
Innovate Pharma

description: An internal email from the Clinical Trial Manager (CTM) to the CRA regarding slow patient recruitment at a specific site. The CTM asks the CRA to review the site's screening log for trends in screen failures and to proactively reach out to the PI to discuss recruitment challenges and potential mitigation strategies.
